subject: Urgent: peak sync window throttle spike -> retry storm
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@syncly.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: ops-team@syncly.com, bryce@syncly.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 04:12:00 -0000
Subject: High 5xx/429 spike during nightly sync (urgent)

Hi Mateo,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood yesterday during our 02:00 UTC nightly batch sync. The job retries aggressively and by 02:10 the throughput collapsed and our consumer service timed out. We've attached a short log snapshot and a sample request-id trace.

What we observed:
- Window: ~02:00–02:15 UTC on 2027-05-15
- Symptoms: repeated 429, occasional 503; per-request latency jumped from ~120ms to multi-second tails
- Customer-side behavior: our batch worker has an in-house retry wrapper around the SDK; initial backoff is fixed at 1s, max attempts 5 (no jitter).

This is causing failed syncs and a handful of downstream alerts. Can Redwood confirm whether you saw a surge tied to our account and whether you have any short-term mitigations (rate-limit exemptions, fallback models, etc.)? We're happy to hop on a call.

Attachments: syncly_20270515_02-00_error_snapshot.log, request-id-trace-7a9c.txt

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Sr. SRE, Syncly Inc.
olivia@syncly.com


From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@syncly.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 04:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike during nightly sync (urgent)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick signal and the logs. We're looking into telemetry for your account now. Initial checks: we did see elevated 429s routed to your model pool at the same timestamps you included.

Two immediate asks to speed triage:
1) Can you confirm whether the batch worker was using the Redwood official SDK or a homegrown wrapper? If official SDK, which version?
2) Please share (if possible) a small snippet of the retry/backoff settings used in the job. The logs you attached show many back-to-back attempts with identical intervals.

Short-term mitigation we'll attempt from our side:
- Temporarily relaxing per-customer concurrency threshold for your pool for the next 30 minutes to reduce throttling while we debug.
- If we find the client's retry pattern is creating amplification, we may ask you to throttle client retries or roll out an SDK patch with jitter/backoff changes.

I've looped in Lauren (Customer Success) and Ben (Account SE) so we can coordinate a call and test plan. ETA: initial telemetry summary in 45–60 mins.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com


From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: eng-oncall@redwood.com
Cc: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 05:10:00 -0000
Subject: Fwd: High 5xx/429 spike during nightly sync -> likely retry amplification from customer SDK defaults

Team — forwarding an active customer escalation (Syncly). Highlights from initial triage:
- Telemetry shows a concentrated burst of ~2.3k requests in a 3-minute period with >40% 429 and ~10% 5xx for the pool serving Syncly.
- The customer's batch worker uses an internal wrapper around the SDK that issues retries at fixed 1s intervals, no exponential backoff or jitter. When many requests hit the same prefix, KV caching doesn't help and we see request fanout that overwhelms the pool.

Attachments referenced in the original email: syncly_20270515_02-00_error_snapshot.log, request-id-trace-7a9c.txt

Suggested immediate actions (please confirm):
1) Temporarily increase concurrency cap for Syncly model pool by +20% for 30 minutes to reduce 429 floodbacks.
2) Enable short-lived rate limiting backoff on the gateway for repeated identical request signatures (prevent immediate replays).
3) Create JIRA INF-1128 to track a longer-term SDK advisory (we should publish recommended retry settings and consider disabling aggressive defaults in older SDK versions).

I'm pasting a relevant snippet of telemetry below for context:
> 2027-05-15T02:03:12Z request-id=7a9c status=429 attempts=3 delta_ms=1000
> 2027-05-15T02:03:13Z request-id=7a9c status=429 attempts=4 delta_ms=1000
> 2027-05-15T02:03:14Z request-id=7a9c status=429 attempts=5 delta_ms=1000

Ben / eng, can you confirm whether the suggested gateway-level short-circuit to prevent immediate replays is safe for other customers?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com


From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@syncly.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 spike during nightly sync (urgent) — remediation plan and next steps

Hi Olivia — quick update and recommended next steps.

What we found:
- Root cause: retry amplification on the customer side. The batch job's retry loop issues immediate fixed-interval retries (1s) for timeout/429 responses which caused rapid request replays during an already saturated window. The effect amplified latency and pushed the pool into soft-throttle territory.

What we did (short-term):
- Increased per-account concurrency cap for Syncly by 20% for two hours (to give you breathing room while patches roll).
- Put a temporary gateway heuristic in place that applies a small, adaptive hold when we detect identical request signatures replayed >3 times in short succession. This prevents immediate amplification while preserving correctness for normal traffic.

Action items for Syncly (recommended):
1) If you can, roll the following changes into your batch worker before the next nightly: use exponential backoff with jitter (initial_backoff=500ms, multiplier=2.0, max_backoff=8s, jitter=uniform). Reduce max attempts to 3 for non-idempotent calls.
2) If you prefer, upgrade to Redwood SDK >= 1.4.2 which contains safer retry defaults (exponential jitter and lower attempt counts). We'll share a short patch you can drop into your CI.
3) Let's run a coordinated test window tomorrow at 02:00 UTC with telemetry open on both sides. Can your team confirm availability?

Attachments: dashboard_peak_window_screenshot.png (telemetry), INF-1128 (created).

If you agree, we'll schedule a 30-minute sync for 02:15 UTC tomorrow to validate the mitigations.

Thanks for the quick partnership. We know these windows are critical.

—Mateo
